summary: Sacks sees Salesforce's 20% drop as likely overdone, calling it a probable buying opportunity while acknowledging soft guidance, because Benioff has consistently adapted to major tech cycles and will likely do the same with AI.
quote: my sense is it's probably a buying opportunity. I mean, I think Salesforce is still a great company. Marc Benioff's a great CEO. He's always positioned the company to chase after whatever the current thing is.

summary: Chamath argues Salesforce is on the wrong side of the tech lifecycle, as AI enables startups to deliver 80% of its features at a 90% discount, meaning large monolithic SaaS companies will lose customers to cheaper, more flexible alternatives over the next 5–10 years.
quote: it is on the wrong side of the life cycle. And the odds are overwhelmingly such that a bunch of small companies will flood this opportunity and provide cheaper, smaller, more flexible capabilities.

summary: Friedberg notes Salesforce's valuation has compressed to ~20x operating cash flow with sub-10% growth, raising the question of whether macro headwinds, SaaS commoditization via AI, or customer hesitancy on generative AI spending are driving the slowdown, but flags that Benioff's founder-CEO status is a meaningful offset.
quote: it's trading at, you know, call it roughly 20 times their operating cash flow forecast with sub-10% revenue growth. And that's basically where treasuries trade... Founders, founders, founders can and will maneuver their way to success.
